CONTACT → SUSPENSION → RIDER

Two tyres. One moving bike.

Launch a hardtail or full-suspension bike over a trail, a square edge or a coarse faceted rock. Distributed tyre contacts drive frame motion, suspension travel and a passive rider guide or moving articulated rider.

Bike & launch

SI UNITS
Drive and braking

Each row replaces all three controls at its time. Positive rear drive rolls forward. Brake values are torque capacities; solved torque may be lower. Times must align to the integration step.

Calculation runs offline before playback. Launch velocity is an initial condition. Grip couples wheel spin and travel through each deformed contact. This is a homogeneous interface coefficient, not a calibrated material preset.

Forces and motion over time

Supported experiment

Both deformable wheels belong to the same translating and pitching bike. Fork, rear linkage and passive rider forces respond to those contacts. Hardtail rear attachment stays rigid. Progressive buffers act before ultimate travel limits.

Uncalibrated and planar, with optional homogeneous Coulomb friction. Soft constraints may creep under sustained load. Authored sharp edges and low-resolution facets are retained. Corner forces remain sensitive to tyre resolution. Hub drive and dry-friction brakes act between wheel and carrier. No frame collision, inflation law, chain/crank model, brake heating, steering, anatomical calibration, saddle support, layered soil or damage. Contact overlap, rim clearance, deformation, pitch and component travel limits stop unsupported motion. No real-time performance claim. Brake holding is regularized, with possible creep; it is not an exact wheel lock. Articulated mode uses independent chassis properties and bounded passive joint domains; it stops before unsupported joint motion. There is no active pumping or manoeuvre controller yet.

Edit complete bike, tyre, terrain and launch scenario

Versioned export includes SI configuration, terrain provenance, body/contact/load frames and support-limit events. Ordered terrain points may include vertical faces and sharp facets. No overhangs; source geometry and tyre resolution are independent. Missing assembly evidence stays unknown. Initial pose is authored; no hidden settling step is applied.
